---
title: Previews, rendered without a phone
version: 1
---

**A preview is a composable with no parameters, marked `@Preview`, that calls the real one with
sample data.** Android Studio draws every preview in a panel beside the code as you type. The
Android CLI from lesson 1 draws them from a terminal, with no device and no Studio, and that is what
this section uses. Here is `CourseRow` whole, with two previews:

```kotlin
// app/src/main/java/com/example/planner/ui/CourseRow.kt
package com.example.planner.ui

import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column
import androidx.compose.material3.MaterialTheme
import androidx.compose.material3.Text
import androidx.compose.runtime.Composable
import androidx.compose.ui.res.stringResource
import androidx.compose.ui.tooling.preview.Preview
import com.example.planner.R
import com.example.planner.data.Course

@Composable
fun CourseRow(course: Course, minutesThisWeek: Int) {
    Column {
        Text(course.name, style = MaterialTheme.typography.titleMedium)
        Text(
            stringResource(R.string.minutes_this_week, minutesThisWeek),
            style = MaterialTheme.typography.bodySmall,
        )
    }
}

@Preview(showBackground = true)
@Composable
fun CourseRowPreview() {
    MaterialTheme {
        CourseRow(Course("kotlin", "Kotlin"), minutesThisWeek = 95)
    }
}

@Preview(showBackground = true, fontScale = 1.5f)
@Composable
fun CourseRowLargeTextPreview() {
    MaterialTheme {
        CourseRow(Course("android", "Android Apps"), minutesThisWeek = 0)
    }
}
```

The string it uses goes beside lesson 1's two:

```xml
<!-- app/src/main/res/values/strings.xml -->
<resources>
    <string name="app_name">Planner</string>
    <string name="welcome">No courses yet. Add the first one.</string>
    <string name="minutes_this_week">%1$d min this week</string>
</resources>
```

`android preview list` finds every preview in a module. `"?:app"` is the CLI's way of naming the
module, `:app`, in the project of the current directory:

```
ana@vm:~/planner$ android preview list "?:app" 2>&1 | tr "\r" "\n" | grep -v Downloading
Build log: /tmp/build-log-3306375368129737089.log
com.example.planner.ui.CourseRowKt.CourseRowLargeTextPreview
com.example.planner.ui.CourseRowKt.CourseRowPreview
com.example.planner.ui.PlannerCardKt.PlannerCardPreview
```

The names are the Kotlin class each file compiles into, `CourseRowKt`, and the function. **The first
run downloads what the CLI needs to render, and compiles the module**; the build prints a line naming
its log file, and the progress bars are filtered out by the `tr` and the `grep`. Then render the two:

```
ana@vm:~/planner$ android preview render "?:app" --fqn com.example.planner.ui.CourseRowKt.CourseRowPreview --fqn com.example.planner.ui.CourseRowKt.CourseRowLargeTextPreview -o previews 2>&1 | tr "\r" "\n" | grep -v Downloading
Build log: /tmp/build-log-15856438888227581378.log
/home/ana/planner/previews/com/example/planner/ui/CourseRowKt/CourseRowLargeTextPreview_0.png
/home/ana/planner/previews/com/example/planner/ui/CourseRowKt/CourseRowPreview_0.png
ana@vm:~/planner$ file previews/com/example/planner/ui/CourseRowKt/*.png
previews/com/example/planner/ui/CourseRowKt/CourseRowLargeTextPreview_0.png: PNG image data, 373 x 154, 8-bit/color RGBA, non-interlaced
previews/com/example/planner/ui/CourseRowKt/CourseRowPreview_0.png:          PNG image data, 249 x 105, 8-bit/color RGBA, non-interlaced
```

```schooling-figure
{"image": "data:image/png;base64,", "alt": "A rendered preview: \"Kotlin\" in a medium title, and \"95 min this week\" in small text below it, on a white background.", "caption": "CourseRowPreview, as `android preview render` drew it."}
```

```schooling-figure
{"image": "data:image/png;base64,", "alt": "The same row at one and a half times the font size: \"Android Apps\" and \"0 min this week\", both larger.", "caption": "CourseRowLargeTextPreview: the same composable with the font scaled by 1.5."}
```

**The second preview is the reason to have more than one.** `fontScale = 1.5f` is what a phone does
when its owner sets a larger font in the accessibility settings, and it is a setting many people
use. Nothing in `CourseRow` fixes a size, so the text grows and the row grows with it: `file` measured
249 by 105 pixels for the first and 373 by 154 for the second, one and a half times in each
direction. Lesson 6 shows
what happens to a row that fixed its height and did not.

## What a preview is not

**A preview runs your composable, not your app.** No activity starts, no `ViewModel` exists, no
network is reached; it draws exactly what the function describes for the data the preview passed.
That is why section 03's stateless shape matters: a composable that fetched its own data would
preview as an empty box, or not at all. Google's documentation also warns that some things do not
render in previews, and names network images among them; lesson 17 meets that.
